title: POC deployment choreography & gate checks
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact, practical choreography for running a customer POC with an emphasis on deployment gates: what we check, when we check it, who signs off, and what the safe rollback/escape hatches are. The intent is a repeatable pattern that Solutions Engineering (SE) can run in 2–6 week POCs with minimal guesswork and clean handoffs to Ops or the customer engineering team.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SE lead, customer technical lead, infra/ops contact, SRE on-call, product manager.
- Scope: Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments where Redwood provides runtime + orchestration. Not a model training plan.

High-level objectives:
1) Validate functional parity for the customer workload (latency, throughput, prompt coverage).
2) Prove cost and scaling assumptions for the intended mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
3) Demonstrate observability and rollback mechanics for production readiness.
4) Provide a clear go/no-go decision and a documented handoff.

POC phases (compact):
- Phase 0 — Prep (3–7 days): contracts, baseline data, account provisioning, flight plan.
- Phase 1 — Discovery & Workshop (1–3 days): workshop to align success criteria, data access, and test prompts.
- Phase 2 — Deployment & Smoke (2–5 days): environment provision, baseline model deploy, smoke validation.
- Phase 3 — Scale & Performance (3–7 days): load tests, batching tuning, KV cache checks.
- Phase 4 — Quality & Regression (3–5 days): prompt set evaluation, A/B vs baseline, stability runs.
- Phase 5 — Handoff & Wrap (1–3 days): runbook delivery, SLA proposal, next steps.

Gating checklist (who signs):
- Identity & Access Gate (SE lead): all credentials provisioned, customer KMS keys mapped (if required), role-based access confirmed.
- Network & Security Gate (customer infra + Redwood SECURITY): VPC peering/firewall rules validated; TLS and cert paths confirmed; audit logging enabled.
- Observability Gate (SRE + SE): metrics pipeline instrumented (latency, errors, token counts), dashboards created, alert thresholds set.
- Performance Gate (SE + customer Eng): 95th and p99 latency within agreed SLOs at target concurrency; throughput meets minimal TPS.
- Data & Privacy Gate (customer legal + SE): PII handling validated for sample traces, retention policy and purge flows agreed.
- Acceptance Gate (customer PO + SE): acceptance tests pass (functional, regression, and UX spot checks).

Pre-req checklist before Phase 2 (deployment):
- Customer API keys or service account created and shared securely.
- Test dataset (obfuscated/representative) uploaded to agreed storage.
- Network routes and egress rules in place; IP allowlist updated.
- Model variant to serve selected and version pinned.
- Resource plan (GPU type, node count, burst allowance) agreed.
- Rollback snapshot plan documented (image IDs, model artifacts).

Deployment choreography (step-by-step):
1) Provision infra (Redwood Dedicated or Private control plane) using the agreed resource plan.
2) Deploy base model artifact with non-production tags.
3) Enable basic logging and synthetic traffic generator in canary mode (low TPS).
4) SE runs smoke tests (auth, simple prompts, embeddings).
5) If smoke passes, open Performance Gate: ramp synthetic traffic to target concurrency with staged increases (25% / 50% / 75% / 100%).
6) Observe anomalies for 30–60 minutes at each ramp level; pause and remediate if error rate > 1% or latency degradation > 2x baseline.
7) Once performance stable, run customer-supplied prompt battery and record outputs (for manual inspection and automated eval).
8) If quality gates pass, flip traffic to customer test workload; run multi-hour stability run.
9) Create snapshot for rollback and tag deployed model as POC-accepted if all gates green.
10) Prepare handoff package: runbook, dashboard links, cost estimate, recommended next steps.

Acceptance tests (examples):
- Functional: 50 sample prompts from customer must return without exception and within 2s for short prompts.
- Regression: BLEU/ROUGE or embedding-distance thresholds against baseline for a curated set.
- Safety: flagged content rate must be below agreed threshold; safety classifier false positives enumerated.
- Load: maintain p95 latency <= agreed SLO at target concurrency for a sliding 1-hour window.

Rollback & escape hatches:
- Immediate rollback: redeploy previous model artifact and isolate new instances behind the routing policy. Document commands/console clicks required and test in a staging run.
- Capacity fallback: route to lower-cost compatible variant (quantized) with automated mapping; communicate expected quality delta.
- Region failover: if regional issues, route traffic to backup region with note about increased latency.

Observability and reporting items to create during the POC:
- Dashboards: latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, token/sec, queue depth, model memory pressure.
- Traces: end-to-end trace for a sample request including network, runtime, and model execution spans.
- Cost telemetry: per-token cost estimate, GPU-hours consumed, and projected monthly cost at scale.
- Weekly snapshot: short PDF with key numbers and notable incidents for stakeholders.

Workshop (Phase 1) sample agenda (half-day):
- 0:00–0:15 — Introductions and POC objectives (SE lead + customer PO)
- 0:15–0:35 — Technical constraints and current infra (customer infra lead)
- 0:35–1:00 — Success criteria and acceptance tests alignment (SE + customer Eng)
- 1:00–1:20 — Data access, privacy, and sample prompts (Data owner)
- 1:20–1:40 — Observability and alerting needs (SRE)
- 1:40–2:00 — Deployment schedule, key gates, and escalation plan

Risks and mitigations (top line):
- Risk: Data access delays — Mitigation: run with representative synthetic data and staggering data onboarding.
- Risk: Unexpected latency spikes under realistic traffic — Mitigation: predefine fallback model variants and aggressive canary ramp with quick rollback.
- Risk: Customer regulatory review takes longer — Mitigation: decouple functional POC from full compliance signoff; document temporary controls.

Handoff checklist (deliverables):
- Runbook with run/rollback commands and contact list.
- Dashboard links and alerting definitions.
- Cost summary and recommendation for Dedicated vs Hosted for expected load.
- Acceptance test results and sample traces.
- Draft SLA and next-phase proposal.

Communications & escalation path:
- Day-to-day: Slack channel seeded (SE, customer-eng, SRE)
- Incident: page SRE on-call and email customer PO. SE lead coordinates triage.
- Executive: weekly 15m sync for exec stakeholders if POC > 3 weeks.

Notes and open questions for this POC run:
- Does the customer require HSM-backed key wrapping for model artifacts?
- Are there downstream services that need rate-limiting enforced at the gateway?
- Confirm whether the customer prefers a hard rollback or traffic-split rollback for the final cutover.

Appendix: quick commands and URLs (examples) — keep in a secure internal doc with exact console commands and non-public URLs.

This doc is meant to be a compact, copy-friendly playbook SEs can use; adapt as required for very large or highly regulated customers.
